title: Electromagnetic tails and the Kerr–Newman Penrose inequality

issues.description: This is not a gap. Theorem 1.1(ii) holds, but only for a nearly trivial reason. With Q_e=Q_b=0 the Kerr–Newman comparison spacetime is Kerr, which has F=0, so no data with nonzero electromagnetic fields can be realized in it. The 'equality without rigidity' conclusion therefore comes from the charge parameters ignoring the EM energy, not from any geometric obstruction.
issues.evidence: The proof cites the dyonic KN potential being linear in (Q_e,Q_b), so F=0 when both vanish, while the constructed fields u^{-6}Ẽ and u^{-6}B̃ are nonzero.

coverage: Read the whole paper (5 sections, about 1250 lines), and checked by hand every computation the main theorem depends on. (1) Seeds: spherical components of Ẽ and B̃ from d(f dφ) and d(h dφ); the cross product dV(Ẽ,B̃,∂φ) = -s²cc' sin⁴θ/r²; all three components of div σ, giving div σ = 2dV(Ẽ,B̃,·) with the factor 2 matching the constraint; the Cartesian expressions, which show smoothness on the axis. (2) Conformal reduction: the weights u^{-2}, u^{-6}; R_g = -8u^{-5}Δu; the coefficients p = |σ|²/8 and ℓ = (|Ẽ|²+|B̃|²)/4, including the polynomial 9t⁴-2t²+1 and the factor 1-t⁴. (3) Elliptic part: the Robin condition u_r+u/2=0 holds for u0 = 1+1/r; the Kelvin reflection gives (RH)(ω)=2N and ∂_r RH=-N, so the Robin condition holds exactly; the Newton potential bounds; the contraction constant CL^{-2}; uniqueness of the homogeneous Robin problem via the reflection extension. (4) Geometry: H(S_r) = 2W/(ru³); W = 1-1/r and W_r = 1/r² for u0, so the stated lower bounds hold; the maximum-r barrier argument (Hessian identity and sign) for outermostness; the calibration β = π*(u(1,ω)⁴ dA) with comass u(1)⁴/(r²u⁴) ≤ 1, using ∂_r(ru²) = uW, and the Stokes orientation; the area bound. (5) Fluxes: m = 2+2N(0)+(1/2π)∫H, checked against Schwarzschild with m=2 and horizon at r=1; the lower bound s²/(3M³L) using only the electric field; J = -4s²/15 (∫sin⁵ = 16/15), with the conformal weights cancelling; J_EM = +4s²/15 (∫sin³cos² = 4/15); the sign in the divergence of the corrected flux, via Cartan's identity. (6) Conclusion: D(1,L) → -1/225; the small-s lower bound on D; continuity in s and the intermediate value theorem; the identity m²-|J| = (A-8π|J|)²/(16πA); the strict branch 64π > 32π/15. Not re-derived: the fine details of the Lemma 2.3 derivative bootstrap (read, plausible), and the topological detour argument for surfaces with edges.
main_claim: Smooth, maximal, axisymmetric electrovacuum exteriors exist with zero charges, a connected outermost MOTS boundary that minimizes area among enclosing cuts, and A > 8π|J|, for which m² < A/16π + 4πJ²/A. Here J is the bare gravitational ADM angular momentum, and the EM fields decay only like O(r^{-2}) with angularly varying tails. Equality cases with no Kerr–Newman realization also exist. The construction is explicit: radial–azimuthal seeds, a conformal factor solved by contraction with a Kelvin–Robin reflection, J = -4s²/15, m → 2, A → 64π, giving a defect of -1/225 in the limit.
sibling_notes: This paper is independent of the other family-260 papers (it states it does not rely on any Penrose or rigidity theorem). It is consistent with the KN Penrose inequality paper at rank 191 and with Khuri–Weinstein: the counterexample works only because J has no electromagnetic surface term and the EM fields have O(r^{-2}) non-Coulomb tails. The conserved total flux J_grav + J_EM is exactly 0 here.
